etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English audience, from Middle French audience, from Old French audience, from Latin audientia, from present participle audiens (“hearing”), from verb audio (“I hear”). Doublet of audiencia.

definitions.definition: A group of people within hearing; specifically, a large gathering of people listening to or watching a performance, speech, etc. [from 15th c.]

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter V, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC, page 26:
quote.text: One saint's day in mid-term a certain newly appointed suffragan-bishop came to the school chapel, and there preached on “The Inner Life.”  He at once secured attention by his informal method, and when presently the coughing of Jarvis  […]  interrupted the sermon, he altogether captivated his audience with a remark about cough lozenges being cheap and easily procurable.

quote.citation: 1952 February, H. C. Casserley, “Permanent Wayfarings”, in Railway Magazine, page 77:
quote.text: My audience to this not-too-easy operation was a small group of Scottish school lasses, who seemed (perhaps naturally) to find the proceedings somewhat mysterious, but at any rate amusing. I wished they would go away, but they didn't, so I had to get on with the job to the accompaniment of a background of giggles!

definitions.definition: (now rare) Hearing; the condition or state of hearing or listening. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1526, [William Tyndale, transl.], The Newe Testamẽt […] (Tyndale Bible), [Worms, Germany: Peter Schöffer], →OCLC, Luke vij:[1], folio lxxxiiij, verso:
quote.text: WHen he had ended all his ſayingꝭ in the audience of the people / he entred ĩto Capernaum.

definitions.definition: A widespread or nationwide viewing or listening public, as of a TV or radio network or program.
A formal meeting with a state or religious dignitary. [from 16th c.]

quote.citation: 2008, BioWare, Mass Effect, Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →ISBN, →OCLC, PC, scene: Citadel:
quote.text: Captain Anderson: Sounds like you convinced the Council to give us an audience.Ambassador Udina: They were not happy about it. Saren's their top agent. They don't like him being accused of treason.

definitions.definition: The readership of a book or other written publication. [from 19th c.]
(historical) An audiencia (judicial court of the Spanish empire), or the territory administered by it.
